item.title: Cartan Dynamics and Limit Sets on Flag Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.17510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical convergence principle describes the collapse of the Riemann sphere under divergent sequences of M\"obius transformations. We develop its counterpart for arbitrary real semisimple Lie groups acting on flag manifolds, and use it to study limit sets and domains of discontinuity of discrete subgroups. The key is to let the source move: the destination of $x$ under $(g_m)$ is the set of all limits of $g_mx_m$ with $x_m\to x$. Our destination formula computes it as the closure of a unipotent orbit, determined by the Cartan data and a bounded Levi factor. The stratified convergence principle organises these destinations into families of translated Schubert varieties attached to boundary points of a compactification of the group. Over the complex numbers, the destination relation is the support of Brion's limiting graphs in the wonderful compactification, providing scheme structures, multidegrees and diagonal intersections. For discrete groups, the union of destination relations determines proper discontinuity and whether a largest domain exists. It relates Quint's flag limit set, Conze--Guivarc'h, Kulkarni and Myrberg sets to the recurrent set, while balanced choices of cells yield domains for every discrete subgroup, without Anosov hypotheses. For symmetric-power actions of non-elementary Kleinian groups on $\mathbb{CP}^N$, we compute the largest domain by a multiplicity bound at points of the classical limit set; for $N\ge3$ it strictly contains the Kulkarni domain, which equals the equicontinuity region. We also obtain nonempty largest domains for Zariski-dense cusped Hitchin groups with unipotent elements, and examples of strongly irreducible groups with no largest domain.
item.dc:creator: \'Angel Cano, Marlon M. L\'opez-Flores, Jos\'e Seade, Andrew Shaw

item.title: Complete Center Classification of a Quintic $\mathbb Z_2$-Equivariant System via Rational Descent and Ramification
item.description: arXiv:2611.17633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a new structural method to completely classify the elementary centers of a ten-parameter quintic $\mathbb Z_2$-equivariant system. The method overcomes the computational bottleneck of direct focus-quantity elimination by combining a Li\'enard reduction, a necessary-and-sufficient analytic involution criterion, and rational descent with residue and ramification analysis. We obtain forty-two explicit original-parameter conditions covering the entire center locus, including all degenerate and boundary cases. Sufficiency is established constructively through integrating factors, first integrals and explicit reversible realizations.
item.dc:creator: Feng Li, Meilan Cai, Chaochao Sun

item.title: Localization for Lipschitz monotone quasi-periodic operators with power-law hopping
item.description: arXiv:2611.17799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove spectral and dynamical localization for quasi-periodic operators on $\mathbb Z^d$ with Lipschitz monotone potentials and power-law hopping. For sufficiently small coupling, localization holds at every allowed phase whenever the hopping decay exponent $r$ exceeds the Diophantine exponent $\tau$. The proof is based on multiscale analysis with exponentially growing scales. We use homotopy in the coupling constant to select the local eigenvalue branches and Schur complement estimates to control the successive elimination of coordinates.
item.dc:creator: Hongyi Cao, Yunfeng Shi, Peizhen Wang

item.title: On the convergence of the False Nearest Neighbours algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2611.18087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The False Nearest Neighbours (FNN) algorithm is one of the most widely used methods for choosing the embedding dimension, i.e. the number $k$ of delay coordinates, in the time-delay reconstruction of a dynamical system from an observed scalar time series. We prove rigorous results on the behaviour of this algorithm for long time series. We consider a smooth dynamical system on a compact manifold $M$ and an invariant probability measure $\mu$. For a typical measurement function and $\mu$-almost every trajectory, we show that the proportion of false nearest neighbours tends to zero (provided that the tolerance threshold is large enough) once $k >\dim M$. On the other hand, for systems with super-polynomial decay of correlations, we prove that this proportion tends to one whenever $k$ is smaller than the Hausdorff dimension of $\mu$. Consequently, in this case, the FNN algorithm (run for long enough time series) returns an embedding dimension $k$ satisfying $\dim_H \mu \leq k \leq \dim M + 1$. This is below the threshold $2\dim M + 1$ required by the Takens embedding theorem, so the classical Takens embedding theory does not explain why reconstructions and predictions with $k$ chosen by the FNN algorithm work in practice. The explanation for this case is provided by a recent probabilistic theory of time-delay embeddings. We apply our results to the H\'enon and Lorenz attractors, showing that the FNN algorithm typically returns $k=2$ for the H\'enon map (in the chaotic case) and $k \leq 3$ for the Lorenz system.
item.dc:creator: Adam \'Spiewak

item.title: Singularly embedded solitons and Stokes phenomenon in the fifth order KdV equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.18102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study embedded solitons (ES) in a fifth-order Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation near a reversible Hamiltonian saddle-centre bifurcation. The solitons correspond to homoclinic orbits to an equilibrium whose linearisation has a pair of real and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. Existence of symmetric homoclinic near the bifurcation is a codimension-one phenomenon governed by a parameter-dependent Stokes constant associated with an inner equation. Using complex matching, we derive an oscillatory large-parameter asymptotic formula for the Stokes constant. This formula implies the existence of a countable sequence of zeros and gives their asymptotic distribution in parameter space. We also develop two complementary high-precision numerical procedures for evaluating the Stokes constant: one based on the late terms of the formal inner expansion and another on direct computation of the stable and unstable manifolds. The numerical results agree with each other and with the asymptotic prediction, confirming both the existence and the predicted locations of the embedded-soliton branches.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Barrio, Vassili Gelfreich, J. Tom\'as L\'azaro, Juan Ramon Pacha

item.title: Periodic orbits of quadratic polynomials of periods six and seven
item.description: arXiv:2611.18231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dynamics of quadratic polynomials is commonly studied by using the family of maps f_{c}(x) = x^{2} + c, where c include C. In this paper we form equations of periodic orbits of periods six and seven on a new (u,v)-plane and consider also the corresponding equations on the (x,y)-plane. The new (u,v)-model produces equations for the periods six and seven with significantly lower degree than the ones obtained by the previous models which enables us to find their solutions.
item.dc:creator: Pekka Kosunen

item.title: Fluctuations of Local Patterns in Non-Periodic Uniquely Ergodic Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.16685v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study various families of non-periodic configurations of symbols assigned to vertices of regular graphs. We restrict ourselves to such systems where considered configurations support a uniquely ergodic measure. Symbols can be interpreted as particles and we are concerned with configurations which minimize the interaction energy of particles, the so-called ground-state configurations. One of the main questions then is whether ground-state configurations are stable with respect to small perturbations of interactions. Such stability may be interpreted as a sort of rigidity of non-periodic structures such as tilings, substitution systems, Sturmian systems, and other uniquely ergodic non-periodic systems. We introduce a property of bounded fluctuations of finite patterns of non-periodic configurations, the so-called Strict Boundary Property. We discuss how relevant this property is for stability of non-periodic structures. Examples of Robinson's tilings, Thue-Morse, and Sturmian systems are presented. Some open problems are formulated.
item.dc:creator: Jacek Mi\k{e}kisz

item.title: Admissibility-Preserving Control for Block Strict-Feedback Systems Under Time-Varying Asymmetric Actuator and State Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.17397v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper addresses the tracking control of block strict-feedback nonlinear systems subject to time-varying asymmetric actuator and full state constraints. To that end, we develop a time-varying Admissibility-Preserving Control (APC) framework, in which the Admissibility-Preserving Input Realization (APIR) generates the plant input through a dynamic realization. The APIR guarantees input admissibility under the moving actuator set whenever each actuator bound contracts slower than the decay rate of the realization, and a closed-form lower bound on its gain is derived. The state constraints are handled by a logarithmic barrier coordinate at every backstepping step, with widths measured from the virtual control to the moving envelope of the corresponding state. We prove that every state lies inside its envelope, with each virtual control only required to remain inside the envelope of the next state, while the tracking error converges to zero exponentially. Simulations demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed safety-critical control scheme.
item.dc:creator: Saurabh Kumar, Lohitvel Gopikannan, Shashi Ranjan Kumar, Abhinav Sinha

item.title: On the Hofer-Zehnder conjecture for Reeb flows without symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.17542v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper continues our investigation of the Hofer-Zehnder conjecture for dynamically convex, non-degenerate Reeb pseudo-rotations of $S^{2n-1}$. The main result of the paper is that, for $n\geq 3$, such a flow has at most $n-3$ alternating prime closed orbits and hence at most $2n-3$ prime closed orbits in total. In particular, the flow on $S^5$ has exactly three prime closed orbits, all of which are non-alternating and elliptic. In addition, we prove that a dynamically convex Reeb pseudo-rotation on a sphere has at least two non-degenerate, irrationally elliptic orbits.
item.dc:creator: Erman Cineli, Viktor L. Ginzburg, Basak Z. Gurel

item.title: A proof of the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture by embedding nilspaces in nilmanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.17567v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every compact finite-rank nilspace admits a continuous injective morphism into a toral nilspace of the same step, and hence into a connected filtered nilmanifold. Combining this embedding theorem with the general nilspace inverse theorem, we establish the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture and extend its conclusion to second-countable compact abelian groups. This yields an inverse theorem for Gowers norms on all such groups, in which the correlating functions factor through morphisms into nilmanifolds. The proof relies on substantial foundations developed in nilspace theory over the past decade, particularly the general nilspace inverse theorem and the representation of compact finite-rank nilspaces as quotients of free nilspaces.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Candela, Diego Gonz\'alez-S\'anchez, Bal\'azs Szegedy

item.title: An accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping
item.description: arXiv:2611.17813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we propose an accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping for unconstrained convex multiobjective optimization problems in a real Hilbert space. The continuous flow is formulated as a system of two first-order equations involving only a single multiobjective projection operator and suitable time-scaling factors. Formally, it can also be expressed as a second-order system with explicit multiobjective Hessian-driven damping, which corresponds to the usual Hessian-driven damping introduced by Alvarez et al. [J. Math. Pures Appl., 81(8):747--779, 2002]. The first-order formulation, however, involves no Hessian term and can be regarded as an extension of the Hessian-driven Nesterov accelerated gradient flow by Chen and Luo [arXiv:1912.09276, 2019]. Assuming that the objective gradients are Lipschitz continuous on bounded sets and that the common lower level sets are bounded, we establish global existence in finite dimensions under suitable time-scaling conditions. An a priori energy estimate confines the solutions to a fixed bounded set, and a Lyapunov argument yields fast decay of a merit function and the KKT residual. Under an additional bound on the time-scaling factors, the trajectory of every global solution converges weakly to a weak Pareto point. Numerical tests illustrate the rapid residual decay and reduced oscillations.
item.dc:creator: Wen Jiang, Hao Luo

item.title: Separability defects in artificial satellite theory: intermediaries, zonal harmonics and secular separatrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.18083v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A five-input Poisson-bracket operator, which reproduces the Levi-Civita separability expressions and is cubic in the Hamiltonian, is used as a diagnostic of artificial satellite theory, in a modified polar-nodal chart regular at prograde equatorial orbits. For the general intermediary proposed by the author in 2020, covering those of Sterne, Garfinkel, Brouwer, Aksnes, Cid and Lahulla and Deprit, the linearised defects vanish if and only if the integrability ansatz holds, the condition for additive first-order Hamilton-Jacobi separation in polar-nodal variables. Second-order defects follow in closed form, and the coupling with the nodal pair comes from the dependence on the physical latitude, shared by the zonal term, Aksnes's intermediary and the originals of Sterne and Garfinkel. For every axisymmetric field the radial defect is linear, with a torque form, and the first-order zonal defect is the operator response to the first-order Lie generator, which also gives the second-order mean radial defect per revolution. In its gauge the long-period second-order average is common to intermediaries without latitude terms. Oblate structures with a displaced centre separate the zonal field exactly if and only if its coefficients satisfy the recurrence of Vinti's translated spheroidal potential, and along orbits propagated over 300 periods in the field truncated at $J_4$ they conserve the approximate third integral better than the centred structure, by median factors of 23 to 77. On secular separatrices the integrated defect is the derivative of the Melnikov function, tested in the eccentric Kozai-Lidov problem, and transverse zero sets of the operator define event surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Martinusi

item.title: All coupling Anderson localization in the quantum kicked rotor model
item.description: arXiv:2611.18320v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study $$\mathscr{H}=\lambda \Delta +\tan\pi(\theta+n^2\alpha)\delta_{n,n'},\ n\in\Bbb Z$$ and prove its Anderson localization for all $\lambda >0$ and Lebesgue almost every (a.e.) $(\alpha, \theta)\in\Bbb T^2$. This conforms in the full measure sense the main assumption of Fishman-Grempel-Prange [{\it Phys. Rev. Lett.} 49(8), 509--512 (1982)] in the study of the quantum suppression of chaos: The pseudo-randomness of the sequence $\{\tan\pi(\theta+n^2\alpha)\}_{n\in\Bbb Z}$ (for $\alpha\in\Bbb T\setminus \Bbb Q$) should result in all coupling Anderson localization for $H$ similar to that for the one-dimensional Anderson model. Our proof is based on nonperturbative Green's function estimates approach using Cayley transform, quadratic Weyl sum estimate and Rellich function analysis.
item.dc:creator: Yunfeng Shi, Li Wen

item.title: Periodic orbits 1-5 of quadratic polynomials on a new coordinate plane
item.description: arXiv:1703.05146v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While iterating the quadratic polynomial f_{c}(x)=x^{2}+c the degree of the iterates grows very rapidly, and therefore solving the equations corresponding to periodic orbits becomes very difficult even for periodic orbits with a low period. In this work we present a new iteration model by introducing a change of variables into an (u,v)-plane, which changes situation drastically. As an excellent example of this we can compare equations of orbits period four on (x,c)- and (u,v)-planes. In the latter case, this equation is of degree two with respect to u and it can be solved explicitly. In former case the corresponding equation ((((x^{2}+c)^{2}+c)^{2}+c)^{2}+c-x)/((x^{2}+c)^{2}+c-x)=0 is of degree 12 and it is thus much more difficult to solve.
item.dc:creator: Pekka Kosunen

item.title: Extensibility and denseness of periodic monoid actions
item.description: arXiv:2502.00312v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A monoid has the periodic approximation (PA) property if, for every full shift on a finite alphabet, finitely supported invariant probability measures are weak-* dense in the space of invariant Borel probability measures. We introduce the class of measure-theoretically extension-compatible (MEC) monoids, consisting of embeddable monoids for which every probability measure-preserving (p.m.p.) action admits an invertible p.m.p. extension. For an embeddable monoid $S$ with free $S$-group $(\Gamma,\gamma)$, we prove that the PA property implies MEC, and that the converse holds whenever $\Gamma$ has the PA property. We establish that every left reversible bicancellative monoid and every finitely generated free monoid is MEC, and deduce the PA property for left amenable monoids that are residually a finite group and for finitely generated free monoids. Moreover, for $S=\mathbb F_d^+$, we characterize the free $S$-group as the unique receiving $S$-group for which all fully supported invariant Markov measures on full shifts on finite alphabets admit invariant invertible extensions.
item.dc:creator: Raimundo Brice\~no, \'Alvaro Bustos-Gajardo, Miguel Donoso-Echenique

item.title: Functional and parametric identifiability for universal differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2510.14140v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mechanistic knowledge of a studied system can be encoded as predictive mathematical models, but this raises the question of what to do when knowledge is uncertain or incomplete. Hybrid mechanistic/data-driven modelling, where unknown system dynamics are learnt from data using machine learning components, is a potential solution. This work focuses on one such approach, universal differential equations (UDEs), and asks when these can learn unknown dynamics from data. We investigate this question using identifiability. We show that UDE identifiability decomposes into parametric and functional identifiability, which concern the model's mechanistic and data-driven parts, respectively. We consider these two types of identifiability along a second, orthogonal, division: structural and practical identifiability, which distinguish ambiguity inherent to the model formulation from ambiguity arising under finite, noisy observations. Specifically, we consider the problem of how to assess practical identifiability for UDEs. As a modelling setting, we use ordinary differential equations derived from chemical reaction network models. Such models arise naturally across systems biology, chemistry, pharmacology, epidemiology, and population dynamics, making them a broadly relevant test case. Through a wide range of examples, we show that chemical reaction networks are a promising setting for UDEs, yielding learnt dynamics that are highly interpretable. We then examine how model properties---including the number of neural networks, the constraints imposed on them, and data availability---affect identifiability. A key finding is that generalising a fully mechanistic model to a UDE can have remarkably little impact on its identifiability. Our results provide strong evidence that UDEs offer an intuitive means of integrating data-driven elements into mechanistic models while preserving predictive capability.
item.dc:creator: Torkel E Loman, Ruth E Baker

item.title: Linear Response for Bernoulli Convolutions
item.description: arXiv:2604.20883v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mu_{\lambda}$ be the Bernoulli convolution measure with parameter $\lambda\in(0,1)$. We study the regularity of the function %We prove that $h=h_{\phi}:\lambda\mapsto \int_{\mathbb{R}}\phi(x)\,d\mu_{\lambda}(x)$ for H\"older observables $\phi$. We describe sufficient conditions for both smoothness and non smoothness of this function. In particular, we show that for almost every function with respect to certain Wiener like measures on $C[0,1]$, $h_\phi$ exhibits a phase transition: it is almost nowhere differentiable for small $\lambda$ and it is almost everywhere differentiable for large $\lambda.$
item.dc:creator: Jianning Fu

item.title: Non-monotone clustering and energetic regime switching in aggregation-diffusion systems
item.description: arXiv:2605.30243v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate transient clustering dynamics in nonlocal aggregation-diffusion systems from an energetic perspective. Starting from a stochastic interacting particle system, we study the associated macroscopic McKean-Vlasov equation on the torus and use its Wasserstein gradient-flow structure to analyse the competition between interaction-driven aggregation and entropy-driven diffusion. Through numerical experiments for locally attractive interaction kernels, we observe non-monotone clustering behaviour in intuitive geometric observables: in particular, the density peak height may first increase and subsequently decrease along trajectories converging to equilibrium. Using the decomposition of the free energy as a diagnostic, we identify alternating aggregation- and diffusion-dominated regimes underlying these transient dynamics. We investigate to what extent transitions between these regimes are related to the evolution of geometric observables, such as the peak height. Our results illustrate how non-monotone transient clustering can arise even in a dissipative gradient-flow system and highlight the complementary information provided by geometric clustering observables and the free-energy-based regime classification.
item.dc:creator: Nathalie Wehlitz, Richard Scherzer, Carsten Hartmann, Stefanie Winkelmann

item.title: On phase-lock area parquet in a special slow-fast limit of model of Josephson junction
item.description: arXiv:2607.26158v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: B Josephson (Nobel Prize, 1973) predicted a tunnelling effect for a system of two superconductors separated by a narrow dielectric (such a system is called Josephson junction): existence of a supercurrent through it and equations governing it. The overdamped Josephson junction is modeled by the family of differential equations on the 2-torus, $\frac{d\theta}{d\tau}=\frac1{\omega}(\cos\theta+B+A\cos\tau)$, which is known as the RSJ model. It depends on three parameters: $B$ called the abscissa, $A$ called the ordinate, and a fixed frequency $\omega$. We study its rotation number $\rho(B,A;\omega)$ as a function of $(B,A)$ and the phase-lock areas: those its level subsets that have non-empty interiors. They exist only for integer values of the rotation number (Buchstaber, Karpov, Tertychnyi). In this paper we study asymptotics of the phase-lock area portrait in a special slow-fast limit, as $\omega\to0$ and $(B,A)\to(0,1)$ so that $(B,A)-(0,1)=O(\omega)$. We show that in the rescaled parameters $\ell:=\frac B{\omega}$ and $u:=\frac{A-1}{\omega}$ the phase-lock area portrait converges to a parquet with boundary lines being parallel to the lines $\{ u\pm\ell=0\}$. Namely, the limit of phase-lock area with rotation number $r$ is the union of an infinite chain of squares going up, with integer vertices and diagonals of length two lying on the line $\{\ell=r\}$, and an infinite strip going down (sector in the case, when $r=0$). We state and prove a generalization of this result to a wide class of slow-fast systems on 2-torus.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Glutsyuk

item.title: Proof of the singularity conjecture for discrete subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$
item.description: arXiv:2609.17506v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mu$ be a finitely supported probability measure on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ whose support generates a Zariski-dense discrete subgroup. We prove that its stationary probability measure on $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{R})$ is singular with respect to the $\mathrm{SO}(2)$-invariant probability measure. The proof compares winding variances on finite covers of a closed hyperbolic surface and uses a topological obstruction.
item.dc:creator: Timoth\'ee B\'enard

item.title: Quasi-equatorial controlled switching in inertial magnetization dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.14069v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We design exponentially decaying transverse magnetic fields for reliable and ultra-fast (picosecond) magnetization reversal governed by the inertial Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation. The control construction uses an explicitly resolvable auxiliary model to select the field amplitude and characterize the influence of its decay rate, with the aim of obtaining reversal followed by relaxation without requiring a precisely timed interruption of the excitation. The auxiliary model is obtained through an equatorial approximation, and bounds on its latitude identify a regime consistent with quasi-equatorial motion. For the full nonlinear macrospin dynamics, an energy argument accounting for both inertial kinetic energy and the remaining field input provides a sufficient condition excluding backhopping, even while the exponential tail remains applied. Approximate confinement times and optimal decay rates are derived from the competition between field decay and inertial relaxation. Numerical simulations confirm the usefulness of these design estimates and identify their limitations near a capture boundary, where nearby pulses can lead to opposite final states. Spatially resolved inertial micromagnetic simulations further support reversal followed by relaxation over the simulated interval and quantify the transient departures from spatially coherent motion. The resulting approach combines explicit pulse design with a full-system energy certificate, while distinguishing rapid initial rotation from safe confinement and subsequent relaxation.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Fortunati, Massimiliano d'Aquino

item.title: Bayesian Transfer Operators in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2509.22482v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Transfer operators provide a linear description of nonlinear dynamical systems by propagating observables or probability distributions. In reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, these operators are represented through conditional mean embeddings, whose regularized estimator coincides with the posterior mean of Gaussian process regression. Building on this correspondence, we formulate Gaussian Process Dynamic Mode Decomposition, a Bayesian transfer-operator method that combines sparse variational Gaussian processes with kernel-based Koopman and Perron--Frobenius operator approximation. The resulting framework provides a principled route to uncertainty quantification, scalable sparse approximations, and data-adaptive dictionary learning for prediction and spectral analysis. Additionally, the model-selection formulation naturally gives rise to a forward--backward operator structure, which establishes a connection between Bayesian transfer-operator learning and time-lagged canonical correlation analysis.
item.dc:creator: Septimus Boshoff, Stefan Klus, Sebastian Peitz

item.title: Auto-differentiable data assimilation: Co-learning of states, dynamics, and filtering algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2603.20891v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Data assimilation algorithms estimate the state of a dynamical system from partial observations, where the successful performance of these algorithms hinges on costly parameter tuning and on employing an accurate model for the dynamics. This paper introduces a framework for jointly learning the state, dynamics, and parameters of filtering algorithms in data assimilation through a process we refer to as auto-differentiable filtering. The framework leverages a theoretically motivated loss function that enables learning from partial, noisy observations via gradient-based optimization using auto-differentiation. We further demonstrate how several well-known data assimilation methods can be learned or tuned within this framework. To underscore the versatility of auto-differentiable filtering, we perform experiments on dynamical systems spanning multiple scientific domains, such as the Clohessy-Wiltshire equations from aerospace engineering, the Lorenz-96 system from atmospheric science, the generalized Lotka-Volterra equations from systems biology, and the two-layer quasi-geostrophic model from geophysical fluid dynamics. Finally, we provide guidelines for practitioners to customize our framework according to their observation model, accuracy requirements, and computational budget.
item.dc:creator: Melissa Adrian, Daniel Sanz-Alonso, Rebecca Willett

item.title: Resonant saddles, tangencies with small spheres, and the characteristic flow
item.description: arXiv:2609.14855v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study resonant Siegel saddles in $\C^2$, with eigenvalue ratio $-p/q$, where $p,q$ are coprime positive integers, through their position relative to small round spheres. An intrinsic invariant $k$, defined through a resonance index that measures approximate first integrals, equals the first resonant obstruction. For $k<\infty$, the maximal contact order with the linear foliation is $m=k(p+q)+1$, and suitably normalized charts give $2k$ tangency circles. We compute their transverse type: resonant terms cancel to first order, and Poincar\'e--Dulac normalization through degree $2m-1$ makes every contact a saddle, while weaker normalization can produce elliptic arcs and periodic characteristic orbits. For the exact model we describe the whole-sphere flow and the correspondence between its tangency circles and separatrix sectors. In arbitrary charts the characteristic return map near a separatrix circle realizes its holonomy, whose $p$-th iterate has, when $k<\infty$, multiplicity $kp+1$, with $kp$ attracting and $kp$ repelling petals. Classical rigidity of resonant holonomy then recovers the analytic saddle class from $C^1$ orbital equivalence near that circle. We also describe tangency loci for arbitrary nondegenerate germs by the numerical range and the leading orbital form.
item.dc:creator: Toshikazu Ito \and Bruno Sc\'ardua

item.title: Range Failure, Resolvent Growth, and Resonance in Partially Dissipative Systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.17712v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We analyze resonance for partially dissipative systems, $\dot u=Au+f(t)$, where $A$ generates a strongly stable semigroup $S(t)$ on a Hilbert space $H$. {Resonance is} the phenomenon whereby a bounded, time-periodic $f$ yields an unbounded $u$, classically occurring when $A$ has imaginary eigenvalues. In infinite dimensions, however, several other resonance notions, introduced here, may occur. Classically, {$T$-periodic solvability} is equivalent to a range condition: $\mathcal{R}(I-S(T))=H$. We describe a hierarchy of range failures, and demonstrate how the growth rate of~$||(A-i\omega I)^{-1}||_H$ dictates a regularity gap between $u$ and $f$. For super-polynomial growth, that gap can be infinite. We demonstrate this phenomenon and its equivalence to the existence of smooth resonant forces. The theory is motivated by a well-studied hyperbolic-parabolic system, which is a simplification of fluid-solid interactions. Our main result shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, the PDE system exhibits smooth-forcing resonance for a dense set of periods. The geometry sharply violates geometric conditions for which finite regularity losses were shown previously.
item.dc:creator: Boris Muha, Sebastian Schwarzacher, Justin T. Webster

item.title: Porosity in Diophantine approximation
item.description: arXiv:2611.00257v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a general framework for obtaining upper bounds on the packing dimension of certain sets arising from Diophantine approximation using the notion of porosity from geometric measure theory. In particular, the framework relies on showing that such sets are mean porous, as introduced by Koskela and Rohde (Math. Ann., 1997). As applications of our framework we show that: For $\varepsilon>0$ sufficiently small, the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing codimension comparable to $\varepsilon^{d}$ up to multiplicative constant. Any $C^{2}$ submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with bounded first and second partial derivatives intersected with the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing dimension strictly less than the dimension of the submanifold. For any matrix $A\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ satisfying certain Diophantine conditions, the set of points that avoid the $\varepsilon \|\mathbf{q}\|_{\infty}^{-\frac{n}{m}}$-neighbourhood of the orbit $\{A\mathbf{q} \mod \mathbb{Z}^{m}:\mathbf{q} \in \mathbb{Z}^{n}\}$ has packing codimension greater than $C_{A} \varepsilon^{m}$ for $C_{A}$ a constant depending on $A$ and $m$ only. \end{itemize}
item.dc:creator: Henna Koivusalo, Benjamin Ward

item.title: Lyapunov spectrum, Harder--Narasimhan filtration and thin monodromy
item.description: arXiv:2611.06388v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the equality case of the inequalities between the Lyapunov spectrum and the Harder--Narasimhan slopes of a semi-simple local system with non-expanding cusp monodromy over a finite-area hyperbolic surface. This gives a nonlattice-transversality alternative of the monodromy group. On the other hand, we generalize Filip's Assumptions A and B to give classes of polarized variation of Hodge structures that achieve the equality. As an application, we recover the thinness of C-32 in $\mathrm{Sp}_6\mathbb{R}$. Besides, we provide an upper bound, called average Cartan spectrum, that dominates the Lyapunov spectrum and study its rigidity.
item.dc:creator: Fei Yu, Junming Zhang

item.title: Extending indoor airborne infection risk modelling to 3D, with local surface deposition
item.description: arXiv:2611.13372v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Mathematical models of indoor airborne disease transmission often rely on simplifying assumptions to reduce computational cost. In particular, aerosol concentrations may be assumed uniform across room height, allowing a two-dimensional (2D) formulation, while particle deposition on surfaces is represented by a first-order removal term acting throughout the computational domain. Here, we investigate how these assumptions affect predictions of airborne infection risk. We extend the Viral Infection Risk Indoor Simulator (VIRIS) [Xue et al. 2024] by developing a three-dimensional (3D) reaction-diffusion formulation in which aerosol deposition is represented by local removal at surfaces through a Robin boundary condition. We compare the original VIRIS framework with the extended model (VIRIS-3D-L) across three indoor spaces of increasing architectural and people-movement complexity: a courtroom, a care home and a supermarket. Across all three settings, the original 2D formulation with global removal predicts lower infection risks than the 3D formulation with local deposition, with differences of up to 50%. The predictions of VIRIS-3D-L also show encouraging agreement with observations from a documented courtroom outbreak previously used to validate VIRIS. Although computation time increases by approximately a factor of four on average, simulations remain feasible on a standard laptop, taking between 7 minutes and just over two hours. These findings suggest that VIRIS-3D-L offers a more physically realistic framework for assessing indoor airborne infection risk without prohibitive computational costs, while the original VIRIS remains useful when rapid simulations are required.
